q: What does the event loop do?
c: Runs queued callbacks when the call stack is empty
t: JavaScript runs on one thread and the event loop schedules callbacks.

q: What is the output order? setTimeout(() => console.log("a"), 0); Promise.resolve().then(() => console.log("b")); console.log("c");
c: c, b, a
t: Synchronous code runs first, then microtasks (promises), then timers.

q: What does optional chaining like user?.address?.city avoid?
